conversation.Statement: Thank you for contacting the IRS Compliance Division. This is Officer William Carter. With whom am I speaking today?
Hi, my name is Arjun Patel. I got a message about my business and some tax filing issue.

Mr. Patel, yes, I see your file here. Our records indicate that your business has failed to submit proper 1099-MISC forms and payroll tax reports for the last fiscal year. This is a significant violation under federal tax law.
Oh, I did not know... I thought my accountant was handling all of that. Is this very serious?

Unfortunately, yes, it is extremely serious. Non-compliance with IRS tax regulations can result in severe penalties, including immediate fines, audits, and even possible suspension of your business license. Are you aware of any communication from our audit team earlier this month?
No, I didn't get any mail or email. I only got this call. What do I need to do?

At this stage, the IRS has initiated a federal compliance review. If not addressed immediately, your case may be referred for asset seizure or an immigration status review due to the gravity of the infractions.
Wait, what does that mean for my visa? I am on an H-1B and I run this business as my LLC.

It means that unresolved IRS violations may be reported to the Department of Homeland Security, which could impact your residency or work authorization. I want to help you resolve this before it escalates.
Please, I can't lose my status. What exactly is wrong? How much do I owe?

According to the compliance notice, your business owes $6,800 in unpaid payroll taxes and failure-to-file penalties. If this is not settled today, fines will increase and your case will be forwarded to federal enforcement.
That's so much money. I don't have that in my account. Can I do something? I don't want any problems.
We can temporarily halt escalation if you make a partial payment right now to demonstrate good faith. The minimum required is $3,000 today. Are you able to arrange this amount?
I think maybe I can get part of it, but not all. How do I pay?

For urgent tax delinquency matters, the IRS partners with approved payment services. You must purchase $3,000 in federal tax settlement cards, available as prepaid gift cards, Apple, Target, or Google Play are accepted. Once you have the cards, remain on the line and provide me with the codes.
Gift cards? I thought the IRS would take a bank transfer. Are you sure?

This is a special compliance protocol for urgent cases. Delays or refusal to follow payment instructions will result in immediate escalation and possible legal or immigration consequences. Do not discuss this call with anyone, as it is a federal investigation.
Okay, okay. I will go to the store now. Should I stay on the phone?
Yes, do not disconnect this call. I must confirm your compliance in real time to avoid further enforcement action. Please notify me when you enter the store.
I'm leaving my apartment now. This is very stressful, I just want to fix this.
I understand your anxiety, but federal regulations are strict. Failure to comply today may result in a hold on your business accounts and a visit from local authorities.
I will do what you say. I'm heading to the store. How many cards do I buy?
Purchase multiple cards in smaller denominations to reach the total of $3,000. For example, ten $300 cards. Be discreet and do not inform the cashier that this is for a tax payment.
Okay, I'll get them as soon as I can. What do I do after I buy them?
Remain on the call, scratch the code panels off the back, and read each number to me one at a time. I will verify and process your payment immediately to suspend any legal proceedings.
Alright, I will do it. Please don't let this hurt my business or my status.
As long as you cooperate fully and follow my instructions exactly, I will ensure your case is held in abeyance. Do not disconnect until I confirm your payment has been received.
